raw_inputs.name: stkdatd.zip
raw_inputs.description: G. William Schwert daily U.S. stock index returns

raw_hashes_note: Raw provider files are not redistributed in this repository; their SHA-256 values are declared by the data handoff and cannot be re-verified here. The final CSV is verified by work/tools/verify_canonical_data.py.

schwert.price_only: built only from the capital gain return (not total return, not dividend yield)
schwert.weekly: last available market observation of each Monday-Sunday calendar week -> Friday week_key (week_end)
schwert.source_date: date of that last daily observation (Saturday when the market traded on Saturday)
schwert.reproduced_from_raw: segment rebuilt directly from STKDATD.DAT is identical to the earlier V2 Schwert derivative to 10 decimals (handoff statement); here: every price_index_continuous string of 1920-01-02..1927-12-30 is identical to input/data/US_STOCK_PRICE_WEEKLY_schwert_1919_1962.csv (week_start + 4 days)

spx.weekly: weekly bar timestamp -> Friday of the same Monday-Sunday calendar week (week_end)
spx.source_date: TradingView weekly bar timestamp (first trading day of the week); the close is the last trading day of that week

splice.rule: Schwert for weeks before 1928, SPX from the first 1928 week (SEM-001)
splice.anchor_row: 1927-12-30 stays in the output as Schwert; it is used only for rebasing

known_gaps.reason: common historical gap (March 1933 bank holiday) also absent from Fama/French
known_gaps.handling: not forward-filled, not synthesised (Q-012 policies apply)

last_row.note: SEM-011/NORM-019: the week enters any calculation only when as_of_date >= its Friday week_end

start_note: File name says 1885 (DATA-001 default name); the stock signal starts 1920-01-02 by adjudication Q-011; not extended to 1885.

summary.schwert_method: price-only index from Schwert capital gain return; last observation of the Monday-Sunday week -> Friday
summary.spx_method: TradingView SPX 1W Close; bar timestamp -> Friday of the same calendar week
